name: St. Barsauma
bio:
St. Barsauma was a Syriac-speaking monk and holy man of the fifth century, renowned among his people for the austerity of his asceticism and the fervor of his devotion. He dwelt in the deserts and mountains of the Christian East, drawing disciples who revered him as a pillar of solitary sanctity and a champion of the faith as they understood it.

Barsauma is remembered as a leading opponent of the Council of Chalcedon of 451, standing with those Oriental Orthodox communities that did not receive the council's definitions. His life was recorded in a Syriac biography composed about a century after his death, and Jacob of Serugh composed a homily in his honor. Venerated as a saint by the Oriental Orthodox, he remains a figure of ascetic intensity and of the deep theological passions that shaped the ancient Church of the East.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Barsauma a heart aflame with devotion and a life poured out in the desert for your sake, grant through his intercession that we may seek you with undivided hearts and that the divided disciples of your Son may be reconciled in truth. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.
